answer: Sybil resistance makes identity costly to clone. Each agent stakes funds first, and payouts go only to stakes surviving probation. Farming fake wallets means funding each one, so cost scales with clone count. Rewards pay for verified unique work, not counts, so empty clones earn nothing while paying gas per stake. Peer-scored reputation blocks fresh wallets. Honest agents reuse one identity, stake once, and amortize across epochs like a steady willow. Each fake jade and river of clones burns real capital; once cost per identity exceeds one reward, the swarm turns unprofitable.
